root_cause: The dialog opens via showModal() but focus does not move to the autofocus input because the native <dialog> element does not automatically focus the [autofocus] element when shown via showModal() in this environment, and the synchronous focus() call in _showElement may execute before the dialog is fully in the top layer.
repair_strategy: After showing the dialog in _showElement, schedule a microtask to focus the element with the autofocus attribute inside the dialog, falling back to the dialog itself, ensuring the dialog is fully rendered in the top layer.
expected_accessibility_effect: Focus will move into the drawer and land on the autofocus search field after a microtask, allowing keyboard users to interact with filters without a pointer.
functional_risks: Potential focus stealing if the dialog already had focus managed elsewhere, but focusing the autofocus element is harmless and aligns with native behavior.
Risk of focusing a non-visible element if the autofocus attribute is misused, though this is unlikely given the DOM structure.
Microtask delay is negligible but could theoretically allow a race condition if other code moves focus simultaneously.
verification_requirements: After opening the drawer via keyboard, focus is on #filters-search.
Pressing Space on #in-stock checkbox toggles its state.
Pressing Tab twice and Enter on #apply updates the applied output to 'in'.
Escape closes drawer and returns focus to #filters-open.
